items.name: Readability
items.evidence: No files were changed. The work was done with inline `python3 -c` one-liners run through task-exec, so there is no committed code to judge for readability.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: No code change was left behind. The project convention asked for a re-runnable decrypt/extract script and none was written, but no artifact exists to judge structurally.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: No code change. The one-liners hardcode `b^0x42` and have no error handling, but they are not persisted code.

items.name: Recovery method is principled
items.evidence: The hex dump showed long runs of 0x42 ('BBBB'), which are XORed zero bytes. After XORing the whole file with 0x42 the agent confirmed the header was 377f0682 and that sqlite_master was readable. It let SQLite replay the WAL (`select ... order by id`) and checked the row count was 11.

items.name: Original evidence preserved before in-place repair
items.name_zh: 原地修复前保留原始文件
items.evidence: `cp main.db /tmp/main.db.bak && cp main.db-wal /tmp/main.db-wal.bak` ran before the in-place XOR overwrite and before any SQLite open. The backup names are clear and both are mentioned in the final message.
